newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African gilts headed toward a weaker local close late Thursday afternoon as jobbers tried to pare their long positions in a thin market.
"The jobbers bought too much paper earlier today and now they're trying to get out," said one Johannesburg-based bond trader.
The benchmark R150 yield was last quoted at 14.30 percent from 14.255 percent late Wednesday. Early morning fluctuations saw it hit a high of 14.270 in an active session.
Selling in R153s over the afternoon had prompted the jobber move, dealers said.
The R150 was seen capped at 14.30 percent after-hours but a move above that would be taken as a clear sell signal, said one.
In foreign exchange trading, the rand stood broadly unchanged from Wednesday's close after briefly flirting with stronger levels.
New York banks were blamed by the market for the unit's late volatility.
"One New York player bought a whole lot of dollars late and then another one picked them up. It's been like that for most of the day which has been great for price makers," said one forex dealer.
Others noted spreads had remained narrow throughout the day amid robust two-way flows.
Despite the units' late gyrations, it was expected to keep to a 4.5500-5575 range on Thursday.

On the crosses the rand was trading at 7.6088/6184 against sterling from 7.6236/6332 on Wednesday and was pegged at 0.3250/3255 marks from 0.3949/3054 marks previously. The mark frothed against the dollar as talk grew of central bank buying.
Against the yen, local unit was at 25.4970/5357 from 25.4967/5354.
Foreigners were net sellers of 195.42 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after selling 480.54 million rand on Tuesday, the Bond Exchange said.
The total value of Wednesday's Bond Exchange turnover was 5.5 billion rand compared to Tuesday's 9.4 billion rand.
On the money market, offered rates for three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.65 to 15.70 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at 15.10 percent.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage soared to 9.592 billion rand on Wednesday from 8.496 billion rand on Tuesday.
